intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that pyridoxine-refractory autosomal recessive sideroblastic anemia-2 (SIDBA2) is caused by mutation in the SLC25A38 gene.

checks.claim: Pyridoxine-refractory autosomal recessive sideroblastic anemia-2 (SIDBA2) is caused by mutation in the SLC25A38 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we define a previously unknown form of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia, associated with mutations in the gene encoding the erythroid specific mitochondrial carrier family protein SLC25A38
checks.explanation: The abstract supports the autosomal recessive form being caused by SLC25A38 mutation. 'Pyridoxine-refractory' is not in the abstract. Only a second-hand summary (Long et al.) says the patients were vitamin B6–refractory.

paragraphs.text: Sideroblastic anemia-2 is a congenital, nonsyndromic, autosomal recessive form of sideroblastic anemia that does not respond to pyridoxine. The sideroblastic anemias are a heterogeneous group of congenital and acquired blood disorders. Their defining feature is ringed sideroblasts: erythroid precursors in the bone marrow with abnormal iron deposits inside their mitochondria (Guernsey et al., 2009). Affected individuals may have severe anemia from birth that requires transfusions (Jardine et al., 1994).

checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in mitochondrial carrier family gene SLC25A38 cause nonsyndromic autosomal recessive congenital sideroblastic anemia.
checks.explanation: The title states it directly.

checks.claim: Sideroblastic anemia-2 does not respond to pyridoxine.
checks.evidence_quote: A son and daughter of unaffected parents had transfusion dependent, pyridoxine-refractory sideroblastic anaemia from birth.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the anaemia was pyridoxine-refractory.

checks.explanation: The abstract states it directly.

checks.explanation: The abstract reports severe, transfusion-dependent anaemia from birth.

paragraphs.text: In a female infant with pyridoxine-refractory congenital sideroblastic anemia, Manabe et al. (1982) found markedly reduced delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) synthetase activity in erythroblasts, with and without pyridoxal phosphate. Mitochondrial neutral protease in erythroblasts specifically inactivates the apo form of ALA synthetase. Both the activity of this protease and the sensitivity of apo-ALA synthetase to it were normal. Manabe et al. (1982) therefore suggested that the low ALA synthetase activity resulted from impaired production of the enzyme rather than faster destruction, which could explain why the patient did not respond to pyridoxine.

checks.evidence_quote: A marked reduction of delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) synthetase activity of erythroblasts was noticed with and without treatment of pyridoxal phosphate.

paragraphs.text: Jardine et al. (1994) studied affected sibs born to unaffected parents. They excluded the ALAS2 gene and showed that the mother was not a carrier of an X-linked sideroblastic anemia mutation. They concluded that the disorder in this family was very likely an autosomal recessive trait. Guernsey et al. (2009) confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance of nonsyndromic congenital sideroblastic anemia caused by SLC25A38 mutations.

paragraphs.text: Mutations in the erythroid-specific delta-aminolevulinate synthase gene ALAS2 on Xp11.21 cause X-linked sideroblastic anemia. In a boy with pyridoxine-refractory congenital sideroblastic anemia, Jardine et al. (1994) found no ALAS2 mutations in the coding region, the intron/exon boundaries, or the 1-kb 5-prime promoter region. They identified a G-to-A polymorphism 220 nucleotides 3-prime of the AATAAA polyadenylation signal, with a gene frequency of 25% among 148 alleles. Segregation of this polymorphism showed that the affected sibs had inherited different maternal ALAS2 alleles, which excluded ALAS2 as the cause of disease in this family. The mother also showed random X inactivation in her peripheral leukocytes.

paragraphs.text: Guernsey et al. (2009) used positional cloning to identify mutations in the SLC25A38 gene in patients with autosomal recessive, nonsyndromic, pyridoxine-refractory congenital sideroblastic anemia who had a normal ALAS2 gene. The mutations included stop codon, frameshift, and splice site mutations. SLC25A38 encodes an erythroid-specific member of the mitochondrial carrier family. Guernsey et al. (2009) showed that the protein is important for heme biosynthesis in eukaryotes. Based on its requirement for erythropoiesis, they predicted that it is an amino acid carrier that can transport glycine.
